mappings.name: scenario: pending on the first status query

metadata.why: `pending_then_successful_walks_the_scenario`: query_status must report what the rail says *now*, not a cached first answer — the poll ladder in docs/flows/reconciler.md is built entirely on that. Each conformance case starts its own container, so the scenario always begins in `Started`.

mappings.name: scenario: successful on the second status query
e2e: a confirm that will settle, selected by MSISDN rather than by reference

why: THE ENTRY POINT of the only PENDING->SUCCESSFUL walk an end-to-end confirm can
reach. The two priority-1 mappings above are keyed on the fixed reference
...0ce0, and a confirm cannot choose its reference: the handler mints
provider_reference_id with Uuid::new_v4() before committing the charge, and a
seam to fix it from a test would be a code path that exists only outside
production (AGENTS.md's first rule). MTN's status query is a GET carrying no
body, so it cannot be steered by a payer either -- which is why the steering
happens HERE, on the POST, and is carried forward by scenario state rather than
by anything in the status request itself.
The same technique and the same justification as requesttopay.json's
'a payer the rail does not know' mapping, and the same documentation-MSISDN
block: 237600000ce0 borrows the 0ce0 suffix from the reference-keyed scenario
it mirrors.
Answers 202 -- the ordinary accepted submit -- because this mapping exists to
MOVE THE SCENARIO, not to change what a confirm sees. worker_e2e.rs asserts a
confirm here is indistinguishable from any other accepted confirm right up to
the point the worker starts polling.
The X-Callback-Url matcher is the same contract requesttopay.json's catch-all
carries and is here for the same reason plus one more: this is the mapping the
settling end-to-end confirms enter through, so a deployment that stopped
telling MTN where to call back would fail the suites that actually watch a
payment settle, not only the adapter-level one.
TWO PARTYID FAMILIES, added Step 9 lane 2b (2026-09-04). `237600000ce0` is the
original: it carries a hex suffix so a WireMock mapping can key on it, and that
is exactly why it is unusable from a real payer. `examples/merchant-demo`
(`Steering::Msisdn`, DEMO_MSISDN) and `frontends/tests/e2e/cypress/e2e/checkout.cy.ts`
(`MTN_E2E_POLL_MSISDN`) both type it directly into a request body they build
themselves, never through a form. `frontends/apps/checkout`'s MSISDN field
cannot do that: `src/lib/msisdn.ts` validates Cameroon E.164 -- `237` + `6` +
eight DIGITS -- and refuses `ce0` as it refuses any other letters, which is
documented there and in `docs/plans/step9-notes/lane-3.md` #4c. `237600000100`
is the digits-only twin that page's form actually accepts: same country code
and documentation block, `100` naming no hex value so it cannot be confused for
one. The `matches` regex joins both into the SAME scenario rather than forking
it, so the walk a payer who typed a real number gets is provably the walk
`237600000ce0` has always gotten -- not a second, only-tested-once path. Proven
directly (not merely by inspection) by
`a_digits_only_msisdn_reaches_the_same_walk_as_its_hex_twin::case_1_settles` in
`backends/tests/conformance/tests/adapter_conformance.rs`, which is what makes
the reachability claim two mappings below -- 'no conformance case sends that
MSISDN' -- no longer true for `237600000100` and had to be corrected there.
The full steering table, both families, is in
`docs/plans/step9-notes/lane-2b.md`.

mappings.name: e2e: pending on the first status query, whatever the reference

why: Matches ANY reference, which is what makes it usable from a real confirm, and
is therefore the mapping in this tree with the widest reach. Three things keep
it from swallowing a conformance case:
1. requiredScenarioState. A container starts every scenario in `Started`, and
only the POST above moves this one out of it. Every OTHER conformance case
sends the fixed placeholder 237600000000 (adapter_conformance.rs, Rail::charge),
which matches neither PartyId family above, so for them this mapping stays
unreachable and their status queries fall through to
requesttopay-status.json's priority-10 catch-all exactly as before. Corrected
Step 9 lane 2b: one conformance case now DOES send 237600000100 on purpose --
`a_digits_only_msisdn_reaches_the_same_walk_as_its_hex_twin` -- to prove the
digits-only twin reaches this exact walk from the adapter, not only from
`examples/merchant-demo` or the e2e spec. That case starts its own container,
same as every other one here, so it does not change what any other case sees.
2. priority 5, below the reference-keyed status mappings (priority 1), so
...0404, ...0f01, ...05aa and the rest keep winning even inside this
scenario -- which is what lets worker_e2e.rs drive a DECLINE through the same
walk by giving the charge one of those references.
3. priority 5 is still above requesttopay-status.json's catch-all SUCCESSFUL
(priority 10), so once the scenario IS entered this mapping is the one that
answers.
4. THIS TREE IS ALSO WHAT `just demo` RUNS. compose.yml:31-32 mounts
backends/tests/conformance/wiremock/mtn into the stub container, so these three
mappings are live for the demo as well as for the integration suite -- one stub
definition, not a test-only copy (the step 4 design's decision 7). The demo
confirms with 237600000ce0 (examples/merchant-demo/src/main.rs, DEMO_MSISDN), so
the POST above moves the scenario to `e2e-submitted`, this mapping answers the
worker's first status query PENDING and moves it to `e2e-settled`, and the
mapping below answers every later one SUCCESSFUL. A demo therefore LEAVES the
container resting in `e2e-settled`: a second `just demo` against the SAME
container settles on its first poll instead of after a PENDING -- that is the
scenario's state, not a change in behaviour. `just demo-down` removes the
container, which is what returns it to `Started`.
Verified by running the conformance suite (26 cases, at the time) against this
tree after adding these three mappings. Step 9 lane 2b (2026-09-04) grew the
suite to 33 by adding three cases that steer this same tree by the digits-only
PartyId family -- see the entry mapping above.

mappings.name: e2e: successful on the second status query, whatever the reference

why: No newScenarioState, so the scenario rests here: every later poll of the same
charge answers SUCCESSFUL too. That matters because settlement is a
compare-and-swap -- a second poll of a charge already moved to `succeeded` must
be a harmless no-op, and the stub has to keep saying the same thing for that to
be what is actually tested.
financialTransactionId is distinct from the reference-keyed scenario's
1234567891 so a test asserting charges.provider_txn_id cannot pass by reading
the wrong stub's answer.
